question.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={e}^{2t},\,y={e}^{4t}+6.$ Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2{e}^{2t},\,{y}^{′}(t)=4{e}^{4t}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4{e}^{4t}}{2{e}^{2t}}=2{e}^{2t}.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2{e}^{2t})}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
